profile.campus: Florence, Boone County, Kentucky (CyrusOne CIN6, part of the Cincinnati metro cluster)
profile.reading:
Per CyrusOne's own campus page, CIN6 sits at 7190-7200 Industrial Road, Florence, KY 41042, just across the Ohio River from Cincinnati, publishing 143,000 sq ft of technical IT space and 5 MW of total IT capacity, with published certifications including PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, SSAE 16 Type II, and Green Globes.

CIN6 is part of CyrusOne's Cincinnati-metro cluster, the company's home market, which also spans Cincinnati proper, Lebanon, and Butler and Warren Counties in Ohio. Wikipedia's CyrusOne entry states Cincinnati Bell purchased a stake in CyrusOne for $525 million in 2010 and divested it in 2015 after CyrusOne's January 2013 IPO; the company was originally founded in July 2000 by David Ferdman and Larry Bursten, and was taken private again when Kohlberg Kravis Roberts (KKR) and Global Infrastructure Partners (GIP) closed a roughly $15 billion acquisition on March 25, 2022. Florence, Kentucky sits in Boone County, part of the Cincinnati-Northern Kentucky combined metro area and served by Duke Energy Kentucky; siting a data center across the state line from Ohio's cluster reflects the same general regional labor, fiber, and power infrastructure available to CyrusOne's Ohio buildings rather than a distinct Kentucky-specific business case documented in available sourcing.

In 2016, CyrusOne purchased the Chicago Mercantile Exchange's original Aurora, Illinois data center from CME Group for roughly $130 million, with CME Group continuing to operate its Globex matching engine on site under a 15-year lease, an illustration of the sale-leaseback and anchor-tenant financing arrangements common among large colocation operators expanding their national portfolio during the 2010s, the same growth period during which the Florence, Kentucky facility was added to the Cincinnati-metro cluster.

reading.body:
CyrusOne Florence publishes 5 MW of IT capacity in northern Kentucky, making it the largest disclosed data center in the state by a significant margin at 52 percent of Kentucky's three reporting facilities.

The facility holds compliance certifications for regulated workloads: PCI DSS for payment card processing, HIPAA for healthcare, FISMA for government, plus ISO 27001 and SSAE 16 Type II. This certification profile indicates the site targets enterprise and regulated-industry tenants rather than hyperscale AI operations. Hyperscale AI training clusters do not depend on these compliance certifications and typically pursue different infrastructure strategies.

The 5 MW capacity could theoretically host roughly 500 accelerators in a dense AI training configuration, though CyrusOne does not specify the actual workload mix. The 143,000 square feet of technical space is published. Kentucky's three reporting facilities total 9.55 MW, placing the state well outside the binding constraints on US AI infrastructure growth. The operator does not disclose full campus capacity or individual facility power allocations.
